newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes end sharply higher with heat.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes end sharply higher with heat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes ended sharply higher Tueday, following gains in the expiring product futures contracts while local spot trade faded.
NYMEX heating oil futures settled 2.27 cents a gallon higher on a short squeeze ahead of the January contract's expiration today.
The rise helped bump up cash prices for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) 55 cents after a sluggish morning.
But the West Coast spot market dried up early Tuesday, as traders left to celebrate New Year's Eve.
With discounts flat at $1.70, Alaska North Slope (ANS) tracked a 55-cent gain in WTI. Outright prices ranged $24.10/24.30 a barrel.
Kern River prices stayed at $18.65/18.75 a barrel after companies lifted postings December 18.
Discounts remained 10 cents below to even with postings, traders said.
Line 63 crude remained untraded off WTI, while the posting plus market was notionally $0.95 to $1.05.
